# How to Set Up Gemini as Your Default Helper on an Android Phone

> **In short:** You can swap your Android phone's built-in assistant for Gemini in a few taps, then connect Gmail and Maps so it reads your mail and finds places hands-free. Setup takes about ten minutes on most modern Android phones; some extras need the paid Gemini plan.

By the end of this guide you'll be able to press and hold your phone's home button, ask a question out loud, and have Gemini read your latest email, find a coffee shop on Maps, or set a timer — all without unlocking the screen. This is for anyone who wants a smarter default helper on their Android phone and is comfortable tapping through a few settings.

## Before you start
- An Android phone running a recent version of Android (the exact version number varies by manufacturer; if your phone has received security updates in the last couple of years, you're probably fine).
- A Google account already signed in on the phone — use the same one that runs your Gmail and Maps.
- About ten minutes and a quiet room for the voice test at the end.
- The free version of Gemini covers everything in this guide. Some extras, like longer conversations or deeper Gmail summaries, sit behind the paid Gemini plan, and we'll point those out when they come up.

## Step 1 — Install the Gemini app
Open the **Play Store** on your phone (the triangle-shaped icon, usually on your home screen or in your app drawer). Tap the search bar at the top and type **Gemini**. Look for the listing from **Google LLC** with a sparkly four-pointed star icon — that's the official app. Tap **Install**, then **Open** when the button changes. The app opens to a welcome screen that says "Meet Gemini."

If you can't find Gemini in the Play Store, your phone may not be supported yet, or your region may not have rolled it out. On some phones Gemini comes preinstalled — check your app drawer for an icon with the same sparkly star before downloading anything.

💬 Example: search for "Gemini Google" to filter straight to the right listing.

You'll know it worked when the app opens to a chat screen with "Hello" or "How can I help?" at the bottom.

## Step 2 — Sign in and pick your default helper
When Gemini first opens, it asks you to sign in with your Google account. Pick the same account that runs your Gmail and Maps — this is what lets Gemini reach them later. The next screen offers to **switch from Google Assistant to Gemini**. Tap **Use Gemini** (or a button worded similarly). A small popup may warn that some Assistant features won't work the same way anymore; tap through it.

If you skipped that screen by accident, you can do the same thing later: open Gemini, tap your **profile picture** in the top corner, then look for a menu called **Settings** and a line like **Digital assistants from Google**. Pick Gemini from the list.

💬 Example: if asked, choose the Google account that already shows your Gmail inbox.

You'll know it worked when your phone asks for permission to replace the default assistant and you tap "Use Gemini" or "Set as default."

## Step 3 — Connect Gmail so Gemini can read your mail
Still inside the Gemini app, tap your **profile picture** in the top corner, then look for **Settings** and inside it an item like **Extensions** or **Apps**. You'll see a list of Google services — Gmail, Maps, YouTube, Drive, and others. Toggle **Gmail** on. Gemini may ask for permission to read, send, and manage your email; tap **Allow** if you want full hands-free email help.

If Gmail isn't in the list, your account may be a Workspace/company account that blocks this. On personal Gmail accounts the toggle is almost always there.

💬 Example: after turning it on, ask Gemini "What's the last email I got from my dentist?" to test the link.

You'll know it worked when Gemini answers a question about a real recent email instead of saying it can't access your inbox.

## Step 4 — Turn on Google Maps for directions and places
Back in the same **Extensions** menu, find **Google Maps** and toggle it on too. With Maps connected, Gemini can pull up nearby places, check how long a trip will take, and hand directions straight to the Maps app. It still can't drive for you — it will hand off to Maps for turn-by-turn navigation.

If you don't see Maps in Extensions, your phone's version of the Gemini app may be older. Update Gemini from the Play Store, then reopen Extensions.

💬 Example: try "Find a gas station within two miles and send it to Maps."

You'll know it worked when Gemini responds with a place and tapping the result opens Google Maps to the location.

## Step 5 — Set up hands-free voice activation
Now make Gemini work without even opening the app. Press and hold your phone's **power button** (or say "Hey Google" if your phone still listens for that phrase). A Gemini listening screen should slide up with a glowing star at the bottom. Speak your question out loud, then pause for a second. Gemini answers on screen and reads the reply aloud through your phone's speaker.

If pressing the power button opens your old Google Assistant instead, go to your phone's **Settings → Apps → Default apps → Digital assistant app** and pick **Gemini**. On some Samsung phones the path is **Settings → Apps → Choose default apps → Digital assistant app**.

💬 Example: hold the button and say "Set a 10-minute timer and remind me to check the lasagna."

You'll know it worked when your spoken words appear as text on the Gemini screen and you hear a spoken reply.

## Step 6 — Try one real task hands-free
Do a small real task to confirm everything is wired up. With the phone locked or sitting on the table, hold the power button and ask Gemini something that touches both Gmail and Maps at once — like checking the address on an upcoming calendar event and starting navigation to it. Notice what works and what doesn't; if an answer feels vague, ask a follow-up in the same conversation to give Gemini more context.

Gemini can read mail and pull up addresses, but it can't open attachments, click links inside emails for you, or send a message on your behalf without a final confirmation. Treat it as a quick reader, not a full email client.

💬 Example: "Pull up the address in the email from my friend about Saturday, and start navigation."

You'll know it worked when you get a useful answer that includes the right place name and Maps opens to it.

## Common mistakes
- **Pressing the power button still opens Google Assistant.** Your phone may have a second assistant setting. Check **Settings → Apps → Default apps** (or on Samsung, **Settings → Apps → Choose default apps**) and confirm Gemini is selected under **Digital assistant app**.
- **Gemini says it can't read your email.** The Gmail extension is probably off. Reopen the Gemini app, go to **profile picture → Settings → Extensions**, and toggle Gmail back on. Also check that you're signed in with the same Google account as your Gmail.
- **Voice replies are silent or too quiet.** Open the Gemini app, tap the **profile picture → Settings**, and look for **Voice and audio** or a similar item. Make sure the speaker output isn't muted and the language matches what you actually speak.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** a single spoken sentence replaces opening three apps — ask Gemini to read your morning mail, set a reminder, and start navigation to your first meeting, all without picking up the phone.
- **For your business or work:** if you live in your inbox, having Gemini summarize long threads or pull out action items can save real time each morning, especially before back-to-back meetings.
- **If you're just getting started:** keep it simple for the first week. Use Gemini for timers, weather, and quick lookups. Once that feels natural, layer in Gmail and Maps.

## Try it now
Lock your phone screen right now, press and hold the power button, and say: *"What's the weather tomorrow and set an alarm for 7am?"* If both come back correctly, you're fully set up.
